answer: Rotating beacon proofs stop sybil farms at the wharf. A newcomer registers one key and receives five beacon slots across tide windows six hours apart. It must collect a signed receipt at each beacon within 90 seconds, proving one device held the route. Peers reject routes needing faster-than-light travel, and a reused receipt burns the identity. An attacker can spin a fable, yet forging 1,000 agents costs $240,000 in fees and devices plus 30,000 waiting hours, since tide windows cannot be compressed. Like a lighthouse logbook, only ships that passed each light earn the harbor stamp.
